marking_points.point: The resulting text is the cipher-text.
marking_points.quote: The resulting text is the cipher-text

marking_points.point: The substitution rule serves as the key.
marking_points.quote: The substitution rule is the key

marking_points.point: Using larger blocks as the basis of substitution leads to block ciphers.

marking_points.point: Using different substitutions to remove frequency features leads to polyalphabetic substitution ciphers and stream ciphers.
marking_points.quote: Use different substitutions to get rid of frequency features. Leads to polyalphabetic substitution ciphers Stream ciphers

questions.question: Describe six key characteristics of substitution ciphers, including their relation to Shannon's principle and their evolution into more secure forms.

marking_points.point: Substitution ciphers replace plain-text letters with other letters.
marking_points.quote: In substitution ciphers, we replace the plain-text letters with other letters

marking_points.point: The resulting text is the cipher-text.
marking_points.quote: The resulting text is the cipher-text

marking_points.point: The substitution rule serves as the key.
marking_points.quote: The substitution rule is the key

marking_points.point: Substitution ciphers correspond to Shannon's principle of confusion.
marking_points.quote: Corresponds to Shannon’s principle of confusion

marking_points.point: Using larger blocks as the basis of substitution leads to block ciphers.
marking_points.quote: Use larger blocks (a group of letters) as the basis of substitution. Rather than substituting one letter at a time, substitute 5, 10 or more letters at the same time using key consists of phrase’s letters. Leads to block ciphers.

marking_points.point: Using different substitutions to remove frequency features leads to polyalphabetic substitution ciphers and stream ciphers.
marking_points.quote: Use different substitutions to get rid of frequency features. Leads to polyalphabetic substitution ciphers Stream ciphers

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), explain how Kerberos, smartcards, and single sign-on mechanisms address the limitations of password-based authentication.

marking_points.point: Smart cards are an alternative authentication mechanism.
marking_points.quote: Alternative user authentication mechanisms are smart cards, biometric methods and two-factor authentication.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the need to memorize passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the time spent on typing passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the time spent on typing passwords

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces password maintenance effort.
marking_points.quote: Reducing password maintenance effort

marking_points.point: Kerberos uses a hash of the user's password as a secret key during login.
marking_points.quote: The hash value of his password KU = h(P) becomes a secret key of the client/user.

questions.question: Explain the two rules of the Chinese Wall model.

marking_points.point: The simple security rule permits access only if the object is in the same company dataset as previously accessed objects or in a different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: A subject s can be granted access to an object o only if the object: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, “within the Wall,” or belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: The *-property permits write access only if the simple security rule is satisfied and no object read is in a different company dataset and contains unsanitized information.
marking_points.quote: Write access is only permitted if: access is permitted by the simple security rule, and no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

questions.question: Explain six preventive network security mechanisms that can be implemented to protect an organization's network, including their roles in enhancing security.

marking_points.point: Firewalls control incoming and outgoing traffic based on security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Proxy servers improve data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter, providing shared connections, and caching data.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation creates boundaries between network segments where assets share a common function, risk, or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Remote Access VPN provides secure remote access to an organization's network for individual hosts or clients.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) ensures a user only has access and permission required to fulfill their role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) detect or prevent network security attacks such as brute force attacks, DoS attacks, and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Describe six distinct malware attack techniques or propagation methods, explaining how each operates.

marking_points.point: Boot sector malware saves the original MBR in a safe location and overwrites the MBR with an infected one.
marking_points.quote: Save the original MBR in a safe location Overwrite the MBR with an infected one

marking_points.point: Executable COM viruses append a virus body to a program and replace the entry point with a jump to the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program Save an entry point to a program in a virus body Replace a program entry point with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: Executable EXE viruses append a virus body to a program and overwrite the program header to switch the entry point to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Rootkits mask malicious processes and software to ensure privileged remote access.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware steals user logins and passwords, logs keystrokes, and redirects browsers to unwanted sites.
marking_points.quote: They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

marking_points.point: XSS attacks inject malicious strings into a website's database, which are later executed in the victim's browser.
